verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西、亚伦说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them,

verses.zh: 「你们晓谕以色列人说，在地上一切走兽中可吃的乃是这些：
verses.en: “Tell the Israelites: ‘This is the kind of creature you may eat from among all the animals[NOTE:1] that are on the land.
notes: Heb “the animal,” but as a collective plural, and so throughout this chapter.

verses.zh: 凡蹄分两瓣、倒嚼的走兽，你们都可以吃。
verses.en: You may eat any among the animals that has a divided hoof (the hooves are completely split in two[NOTE:1]) and that also chews the cud.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “every divider of hoof and cleaver of the cleft of hooves”; KJV, ASV “parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted.”

Heb “bringer up of the cud” (a few of the ancient versions include the conjunction “and,” but it does not appear in the MT). The following verses make it clear that both dividing the hoof and chewing the cud were required; one of these conditions would not be enough to make the animal suitable for eating without the other.

verses.zh: 但那倒嚼或分蹄之中不可吃的乃是：骆驼―因为倒嚼不分蹄，就与你们不洁净；
verses.en: However, you must not eat these[NOTE:1] from among those that chew the cud and have divided hooves: The camel is unclean to you[NOTE:2] because it chews the cud[NOTE:3] even though its hoof is not divided.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “this,” but as a collective plural (see the following context).
Regarding “clean” versus “unclean,” see the note on Lev 10:10.
Heb “because a chewer of the cud it is” (see also vv. 5 and 6).
Heb “and hoof there is not dividing” (see also vv. 5 and 6).

verses.zh: 沙番―因为倒嚼不分蹄，就与你们不洁净；
verses.en: The rock badger[NOTE:1] is unclean to you because it chews the cud even though its hoof is not divided.
notes: A small animal generally understood to be Hyrax syriacus; KJV, ASV, NIV84 “coney”; NIV11 “hyrax”; NKJV “rock hyrax.”

verses.zh: 兔子―因为倒嚼不分蹄，就与你们不洁净；
verses.en: The hare is unclean to you because it chews the cud even though its hoof is not divided.

verses.zh: 猪―因为蹄分两瓣，却不倒嚼，就与你们不洁净。
verses.en: The pig is unclean to you because its hoof is divided (the hoof is completely split in two[NOTE:1]) , even though it does not chew the cud.[NOTE:2]
notes: See the note on Lev 11:3.

The meaning and basic rendering of this clause is quite certain, but the verb for “chewing” the cud here is not the same as the preceding verses, where the expression is “to bring up the cud” (see the note on v. 3 above). It appears to be a cognate verb for the noun “cud” (גֵּרָה, gerah) and could mean either “to drag up” (i.e., from the Hebrew Qal of גָרָר [garar] meaning “to drag,” referring to the dragging the cud up and down between the stomach and mouth of the ruminant animal; so J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:647, 653) or “to chew” (i.e., from the Hebrew Niphal [or Qal B] of גָרָר used in a reciprocal sense; so J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 149, and compare BDB 176 s.v. גָרַר, “to chew,” with HALOT 204 s.v. גרר qal. B, “to ruminate”).

verses.zh: 这些兽的肉，你们不可吃；死的，你们不可摸，都与你们不洁净。
verses.en: You must not eat from their meat, and you must not touch their carcasses;[NOTE:1] they are unclean to you.
notes: The regulations against touching the carcasses of dead unclean animals (contrast the restriction against eating their flesh) is treated in more detail in Lev 11:24-28 (cf. also vv. 29-40). For the time being, this chapter continues to develop the issue of what can and cannot be eaten.

verses.zh: 「水中可吃的乃是这些：凡在水里、海里、河里、有翅有鳞的，都可以吃。
verses.en: “‘These you can eat from all creatures that are in the water: Any creatures in the water that have both fins and scales,[NOTE:1] whether in the seas or in the streams,[NOTE:2] you may eat.
notes: Heb “all which have fin and scale” (see also vv. 10 and 12).
Heb “in the water, in the seas and in the streams” (see also vv. 10 and 12).

verses.zh: 凡在海里、河里，并一切水里游动的活物，无翅无鳞的，你们都当以为可憎。
verses.en: But any creatures that do not have both fins and scales, whether in the seas or in the streams, from all the swarming things of the water and from all the living creatures that are in the water, are detestable to you.

verses.zh: 这些无翅无鳞、以为可憎的，你们不可吃它的肉；死的也当以为可憎。
verses.en: Since they are detestable to you, you must not eat their meat, and their carcass you must detest.

verses.zh: 凡水里无翅无鳞的，你们都当以为可憎。
verses.en: Any creature in the water that does not have both fins and scales is detestable to you.

verses.zh: 「雀鸟中你们当以为可憎、不可吃的乃是：雕、狗头雕、红头雕、
verses.en: “‘These you are to detest from among the birds—they must not be eaten, because they are detestable:[NOTE:1] the griffon vulture, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
notes: For zoological remarks on the following list of birds see J. Milgrom, Leviticus (AB), 1:662-64; and J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 159-60.

verses.zh: 鹞鹰、小鹰与其类；
verses.en: the kite, the buzzard of any kind,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the buzzard to its kind” (see also vv. 16 and 19 for the same expression “of any kind”).

verses.zh: 乌鸦与其类；
verses.en: every kind of crow,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “every crow to its kind.” Many English versions (e.g., KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT) render this as “raven.”

verses.zh: 鸵鸟、夜鹰、鱼鹰、鹰与其类；
verses.en: the eagle owl,[NOTE:1] the short-eared owl, the long-eared owl, the hawk of any kind,
notes: Literally, “the daughter of the wasteland.” Various proposals for the species of bird referred to here include “owl” (KJV), “horned owl” (NIV, NCV), and “ostrich” (ASV, NAB, NASB, NRSV, NLT).

verses.zh: 鴞鸟、鸬鹚、猫头鹰、
verses.en: the little owl, the cormorant, the screech owl,

verses.zh: 角鸱、鹈鹕、秃雕、
verses.en: the white owl, the scops owl, the osprey,

verses.zh: 鹳、鹭鸶与其类；戴鵀与蝙蝠。
verses.en: the stork, the heron of any kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.

verses.zh: 「凡有翅膀用四足爬行的物，你们都当以为可憎。
verses.en: “‘Every winged swarming thing that walks on all fours[NOTE:1] is detestable to you.
notes: Heb “the one walking on four” (cf. vv. 21-23 and 27-28).

verses.zh: 只是有翅膀用四足爬行的物中，有足有腿，在地上蹦跳的，你们还可以吃。
verses.en: However, this you may eat from all the winged swarming things that walk on all fours, which have jointed legs[NOTE:1] to hop with on the land.
notes: Heb “which to it are lower legs from above to its feet” (reading the Qere “to it” rather than the Kethib “not”).

verses.zh: 其中有蝗虫、蚂蚱、蟋蟀与其类；蚱蜢与其类；这些你们都可以吃。
verses.en: These you may eat from them:[NOTE:1] the locust of any kind, the bald locust of any kind, the cricket of any kind, the grasshopper of any kind.
notes: For entomological remarks on the following list of insects see J. Milgrom, Leviticus (AB), 1:665-66; and J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 160-61.

verses.zh: 但是有翅膀有四足的爬物，你们都当以为可憎。
verses.en: But any other winged swarming thing that has four legs is detestable to you.

verses.zh: 「这些都能使你们不洁净。凡摸了死的，必不洁净到晚上。
verses.en: “‘By these[NOTE:1] you defile yourselves—anyone who touches their carcass will be unclean until the evening,
notes: Heb “and to these.”

verses.zh: 凡拿了死的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服。
verses.en: and anyone who carries their carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until the evening.

verses.zh: 凡走兽分蹄不成两瓣、也不倒嚼的，是与你们不洁净；凡摸了的就不洁净。
verses.en: “‘All[NOTE:1] animals that divide the hoof, but it is not completely split in two,[NOTE:2] and do not chew the cud[NOTE:3] are unclean to you; anyone who touches them becomes unclean.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “to all” (cf. the note on v. 24). This and the following verses develop more fully the categories of uncleanness set forth in principle in vv. 24-25.
Heb “divides hoof and cleft it does not cleave”; KJV “divideth the hoof, and is not clovenfooted”; NLT “divided but unsplit hooves.”
See the note on Lev 11:3.
Compare the regulations in Lev 11:2-8.

verses.zh: 凡四足的走兽，用掌行走的，是与你们不洁净；摸其尸的，必不洁净到晚上。
verses.en: All that walk on their paws among all the creatures that walk on all fours[NOTE:1] are unclean to you. Anyone who touches their carcass will be unclean until the evening,
notes: Heb “the one walking on four.” Cf. Lev 11:20-23.

verses.zh: 拿其尸的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服。这些是与你们不洁净的。
verses.en: and the one who carries their carcass must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening; they are unclean to you.

verses.zh: 「地上爬物与你们不洁净的乃是这些：鼬鼠、鼫鼠、蜥蜴与其类；
verses.en: “‘Now this is what is unclean to you among the swarming things that swarm on the land:[NOTE:1] the rat, the mouse, the large lizard of any kind,
notes: For zoological analyses of the list of creatures in vv. 29-30, see J. Milgrom, Leviticus (AB), 1:671-72; and J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 161-62.

verses.zh: 壁虎、龙子、守宫、蛇医、蝘蜓。
verses.en: the Mediterranean gecko, the spotted lizard, the wall gecko, the skink, and the chameleon.

verses.zh: 这些爬物都是与你们不洁净的。在它死了以后，凡摸了的，必不洁净到晚上。
verses.en: These are the ones that are unclean to you among all the swarming things. Anyone who touches these creatures[NOTE:1] when they die will be unclean until evening.
notes: Heb “touches them.”

verses.zh: 其中死了的，掉在甚么东西上，这东西就不洁净，无论是木器、衣服、皮子、口袋，不拘是做甚么工用的器皿，须要放在水中，必不洁净到晚上，到晚上才洁净了。
verses.en: Also, anything they fall on[NOTE:1] when they die will become unclean—any wood vessel or garment or article of leather or sackcloth. Any such vessel with which work is done must be immersed in water[NOTE:2] and will be unclean until the evening. Then it will become clean.
notes: Heb “And all which it shall fall on it from them.”
Heb “in water it shall be brought.”

verses.zh: 若有死了掉在瓦器里的，其中不拘有甚么，就不洁净，你们要把这瓦器打破了。
verses.en: As for any clay vessel they fall into,[NOTE:1] everything in it[NOTE:2] will become unclean, and you must break it.
notes: Heb “And any earthenware vessel which shall fall from them into its midst.”
Heb “all which is in its midst.”

verses.zh: 其中一切可吃的食物，沾水的就不洁净，并且那样器皿中一切可喝的，也必不洁净。
verses.en: Any food that may be eaten which becomes soaked with water[NOTE:1] will become unclean. Anything drinkable[NOTE:2] in any such vessel will become unclean.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “which water comes on it.”
Heb “any drink which may be drunk”; NASB “any liquid which may be drunk”; NLT “any beverage that is in such an unclean container.”
This half of the verse assumes that the unclean carcass has fallen into the food or drink (cf. v. 33 and also vv. 35-38).

verses.zh: 其中已死的，若有一点掉在甚么物件上，那物件就不洁净，不拘是炉子，是锅台，就要打碎，都不洁净，也必与你们不洁净。
verses.en: Anything their carcass may fall on will become unclean. An oven or small stove must be smashed to pieces; they are unclean, and they will stay unclean[NOTE:1] to you.
notes: Heb “be unclean.”

verses.zh: 但是泉源或是聚水的池子仍是洁净；惟挨了那死的，就不洁净。
verses.en: However, a spring or a cistern which collects water[NOTE:1] will be clean, but one who touches the creature’s carcass will be unclean.
notes: Heb “a spring and a cistern collection of water”; NAB, NIV “for collecting water.”

verses.zh: 若是死的，有一点掉在要种的子粒上，子粒仍是洁净；
verses.en: Now, if such a carcass falls on any sowing seed which is to be sown,[NOTE:1] it is clean,
notes: Heb “And if there falls from their carcass on any seed of sowing which shall be sown.”

verses.zh: 若水已经浇在子粒上，那死的有一点掉在上头，这子粒就与你们不洁净。
verses.en: but if water is put on the seed and such a carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.

verses.zh: 「你们可吃的走兽若是死了，有人摸它，必不洁净到晚上；
verses.en: “‘Now if an animal[NOTE:1] that you may eat dies,[NOTE:2] whoever touches its carcass will be unclean until the evening.
notes: This word for “animal” refers to land animal quadrupeds, not just any beast that dwells on the land (cf. 11:2).
Heb “which is food for you” or “which is for you to eat.”

verses.zh: 有人吃那死了的走兽，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服；拿了死走兽的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服。
verses.en: One who eats from its carcass must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening, and whoever carries its carcass must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening.

verses.zh: 「凡地上的爬物是可憎的，都不可吃。
verses.en: Every swarming thing that swarms on the land is detestable; it must not be eaten.

verses.zh: 凡用肚子行走的和用四足行走的，或是有许多足的，就是一切爬在地上的，你们都不可吃，因为是可憎的。
verses.en: You must not eat anything that crawls[NOTE:1] on its belly or anything that walks on all fours or on any number of legs[NOTE:2] of all the swarming things that swarm on the land, because they are detestable.
notes: Heb “goes” (KJV, ASV “goeth”); NIV11 “moves along”; NLT “slither along.” The same Hebrew term is translated “walks” in the following clause.
Heb “until all multiplying of legs.”

verses.zh: 你们不可因甚么爬物使自己成为可憎的，也不可因这些使自己不洁净，以致染了污秽。
verses.en: Do not make yourselves detestable by any of the swarming things.[NOTE:1] You must not defile yourselves by them and become unclean by them,
notes: Heb “by any of the swarming things that swarm.”

verses.zh: 我是耶和华―你们的　神；所以你们要成为圣洁，因为我是圣洁的。你们也不可在地上的爬物污秽自己。
verses.en: for I am the Lord your God, and you are to sanctify yourselves and be holy because I am holy. You must not defile yourselves by any of the swarming things that creep on the ground,

verses.zh: 我是把你们从埃及地领出来的耶和华，要作你们的　神；所以你们要圣洁，因为我是圣洁的。」
verses.en: for I am the Lord who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God,[NOTE:1] and you are to be holy because I am holy.
notes: Heb “to be to you for a God.”

verses.zh: 这是走兽、飞鸟，和水中游动的活物，并地上爬物的条例。
verses.en: This is the law[NOTE:1] of the land animals, the birds, all the living creatures that move in the water, and all the creatures[NOTE:2] that swarm on the land,
notes: The Hebrew term translated “law” (תּוֹרָה, torah) introduces here a summary or colophon for all of Lev 11. Similar summaries are found in Lev 7:37-38; 13:59; 14:54-57; and 15:32-33.
Heb “for all the creatures.”

verses.zh: 要把洁净的和不洁净的，可吃的与不可吃的活物，都分别出来。
verses.en: to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between the living creatures that may be eaten and the living creatures that must not be eaten.’”
